children: By Avinash  P

Canada's benchmark stock index inched higher on Tuesday, with utilities leading gains, as a pullback in global bond yields and easing oil prices supported sentiment, although weakness in energy and mining shares capped advances.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index
rose 0.19% to 35,587.45 points by 10:08 a.m. ET and was on track for its third straight day of gains.
Utilities
rose 1%, leading gains, as global bond yields retreated
Emera
said it would acquire Canadian Utilities
in an all-stock deal worth C$14.3 billion ($10.02 billion), creating one of Canada's largest utilities
Emera fell 2%, while Canadian Utilities inched higher marginally. ATCO
jumped 12.8% after saying it would spin off into a standalone publicly traded industrial services company called New ATCO
Oil fell by more than $2 as rising Middle Eastern crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release eased supply concerns, with Brent Crude
dipping below $100 a barrel
The energy sector
fell 1.4%, while the materials sector
dropped 0.7%, limiting broader market gains
The yield on the US benchmark 10-year Treasury note
dipped after hitting a 24-year high on Monday, while the yield on the Canadian 10-year government bond (CA10YT=RR) also edged lower, offering some respite to markets
"I'd be focused more on interest rates, the 10-year yield in the United States, than I would be on energy prices, although they're related," said Matt Skipp, president at SW8 Asset Management
"A moderating oil price seems to have the potential to lower yields, as investors worry less about inflation," Skipp added
Concerns over persistent inflation and rising government debt, however, continue to keep bond and equity markets on edge
Markets are pricing in at least one more quarter-point rate hike from the US Federal Reserve and a 25-basis-point increase from the Bank of Canada before year-end, according to LSEG compiled data

title: Canada's TSX edges up as bond yields retreat, utility shares advance
